capabilities: home-inventory | Records household items in nested locations with tags, quantities, purchase, warranty and maintenance details and attached photos or documents, through a web interface and a REST API.
description:
UnitySVC runs the official Homebox image (the upstream rootless variant) in a separate container for each enrollment, with its own HTTPS address. Homebox is a self-hosted home inventory: record your belongings as items in nested locations, with tags, quantities, serial and model numbers, purchase and warranty details, maintenance logs, and attached photos, receipts and manuals. It prints QR-code labels, imports and exports CSV, reports totals by location and tag, and has a REST API with personal API keys. Everything is kept in the instance's own SQLite database and attachment files, stored in the `homebox` folder of your home, so it survives stopping the instance and even removing it and enrolling again.

Enroll in the base channel and keep the generated API key pepper. Homebox has no administrator account set from the enrollment: open `https://<instance>/` and register your own account with an email and password. Registration is open until you close it, so anyone who finds the address can create an account of their own, in a separate collection that cannot see yours; after registering, set **Allow registration** to `false` to stop that. You can run one Homebox instance at a time. See How to use this service for full setup and limitations.

You pay the selected channel's platform compute cost while the instance runs, including idle time, and the platform keeps the data in your home while it is stopped. Labs adds no markup and receives no seller payout. See the upstream Homebox documentation and issue tracker for software-specific help.

features: Items in nested locations, with tags, quantities and custom fields

Your data is kept in your home, across stops, restarts and re-enrollment

HBOX_AUTH_API_KEY_PEPPER.description: A server-side secret that Homebox mixes into the stored hashes of the API keys you create; Homebox refuses to start without one of at least 32 characters. Generated for this enrollment; keep it or enter your own. It is not a sign-in password: you sign in with the account you register. It must stay the same for as long as you use the data: if it changes, every API key created before stops working (passwords and the inventory are not affected). Because your data lives in your home and outlasts the enrollment, enter the same value when you enroll again; a new enrollment otherwise generates a different one. Save it now: the platform keeps it as a secret and does not show it again.
HBOX_AUTH_API_KEY_PEPPER.title: API key pepper

HBOX_OPTIONS_ALLOW_REGISTRATION.description: Whether anyone who can reach the address may register an account. Homebox has no administrator account set from the enrollment, so this starts as true: open the instance and register your own account first. While it is true, anyone who finds the address can also register; each registration gets its own separate collection and cannot see yours, but it uses your instance and storage. After you have registered, set this to false and save; changing it restarts the instance and keeps your data. With false, existing accounts still sign in, and a collection owner can still invite people with an invitation link.
HBOX_OPTIONS_ALLOW_REGISTRATION.title: Allow registration
